The Last Pocket now opens with a new group-portrait title screen: the smiling hero in front of the rival cast beneath an illustrated gold title. Defeating the final rival presents the World Champion trophy, the player's name and their final points, followed by the final result and optional score-sharing choice.

The global AI Championship top 100 is live at https://lastpocket.quietbytehq.uk. A completed run claims the World Champion / All 48 rivals defeated badge. Each public name ranks once by its highest score; a completed-run badge survives a later higher unfinished score. Local-versus games are excluded. Minimum 1,000 points; points must be multiples of 50.

Posting is explicit and optional. The share screen names the destination and four fields sent: chosen name, points, run category and version. F2/gamepad X toggles a remembered local-only setting; Escape/B keeps the result local. No score history or save slots are uploaded. Offline posts are dropped without interrupting play. Manual tournament saves remain local and unchanged.

Scores and champion claims are self-reported, not verified. Fake scores and name impersonation remain possible. Server name/range checks, a salted-address submission limit and private moderation reduce junk; they do not prove gameplay.

Validation: 19,628 source assertions, 19 local Worker checks, 9 new native input checks and 55 compiled Linux runtime checks passed. Measured at 1920×1080 on the development Intel GPU: pool 59.64 fps, snooker 60.00 fps and GOAT AI 59.39 fps. Live normal/game champion submission, badge display and admin removal passed; the board was left empty. The game test simulated a completed result rather than manually playing all 48 frames.

Linux x86-64, offline gameplay with optional online scores. Source and original artwork: Apache-2.0; bundled media retains NOTICE terms. Gamepad access in Snap: `sudo snap connect the-last-pocket:joystick`.
